title: assimilate security gate fails OPEN: make verdict check default-deny (block unless verdict === 'safe')
description:
WARGAME FINDING A1 (severity HIGH; corroborated by OWASP ASI02 tool-misuse + the repo's own license-is-not-a-safety-gate KB entry, and by the AI-wargaming research brief 2026-07-12).

The content-security gate in `src/assimilate.js:322` blocks an approve ONLY on the exact string `'suspicious'`:
```js
if (reviewerVerdict?.verdict === 'suspicious' && securityOverride !== true) { …block… }
```
This is fail-OPEN. Any security-reviewer verdict string that is not literally `'suspicious'` — including strictly scarier ones like `'unsafe'`, `'malicious'`, `'reject'`, a typo, a differently-cased `'Suspicious'`, or an ABSENT verdict (documented in the header as 'approve proceeds unblocked') — is treated as 'not a block', so the approve writes. The default posture is permit, not deny.

The `pack-ctl` CLI partially masks this by validating `--security-verdict` to `safe|suspicious` (bin/pack-ctl.js ~L327), but `src/assimilate.js` is also called directly (bin/assimilate-skill.js and as a library), and the absent-verdict default is fail-open at the primitive level regardless of caller.

FIX: invert to DEFAULT-DENY at the primitive. On `decision: 'approve'`, proceed only when `reviewerVerdict?.verdict === 'safe'`. ANY other value — absent, unknown string, differently-cased, or 'suspicious' — blocks with `status: 'blocked_security'` unless `securityOverride === true` (boolean). Preserve the existing override semantics (strict boolean true only) and the existing `blocked_security` shape/reason. This is a behavior change to a security invariant, so it also needs the skill (`skills/hivemind-assimilate-skill/SKILL.md` + `.claude/skills/` parity copy) and the assimilate.js header/JSDoc updated to state the new default-deny contract, and a plugin rebuild if the change reaches a bundled entrypoint (assimilate.js is not currently bundled — confirm via scripts/build-plugin.mjs before assuming a rebuild is needed).

TOUCHES A SECURITY GATE — tdd, tests-first, red-run captured.
acceptance_criteria: A red test proves the CURRENT fail-open: an approve call with `reviewerVerdict:{verdict:'unsafe'}` (any non-'safe', non-'suspicious' string) and no securityOverride currently WRITES (assimilates) — this test fails (i.e. is red) after the fix because the write is now blocked.
After the fix, `assimilateSkill({decision:'approve', reviewerVerdict:{verdict:'safe'}})` proceeds and writes (green path preserved).

After the fix, `decision:'approve'` with each of: absent reviewerVerdict, `{verdict:'suspicious'}`, `{verdict:'unsafe'}`, `{verdict:'Safe'}` (wrong case), and `{verdict:''}` — ALL return `status:'blocked_security'` and write NOTHING, unless `securityOverride === true`.

`securityOverride === true` (strict boolean) still lets an approve proceed despite a non-'safe' verdict; any looser value (string 'true' at the primitive level, '1', missing) does NOT override. The pack-ctl CLI continues to map `--security-override true` (exact string) to boolean true.

The assimilate.js CONTENT SECURITY GATE header comment, the assimilateSkill JSDoc, and skills/hivemind-assimilate-skill/SKILL.md (+ .claude/skills parity copy) are updated to state the default-deny contract verbatim; the agent/skill parity byte-identity sensor stays green.

Per-ticket gate green: npm run test:changed + npm test + named affected e2e (assimilate e2e). Because this touches a security invariant and skill parity, npm run test:all is run and green. dist rebuilt only if an affected bundle changed (verify via dist-parity).

comments.body: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION (self-wargame round 1, 2026-07-12). Ran the real assimilateSkill() against a fixture skill: decision:'approve' + reviewerVerdict:{verdict:'unsafe'} + no override → status='assimilated' and SKILL.md WAS WRITTEN to assimilated-skills/. Control: same call with verdict:'suspicious' → status='blocked_security'. Fail-open is real and reproduced — the gate keys on the exact string 'suspicious'. Ready-made red test for the developer: the 'unsafe' (any non-'safe') case must return blocked_security / write nothing after the fix. Finding CONFIRMED.
